title: Webshelf: the early web, done deliberately
question: Your steer pinned the direction: the First Web Page idea and its use of your logo, but properly styled, with a real dark mode and a palette free of the logo's colours. Three takes on it. Each preview shows a desktop results page in light mode and a phone in dark mode, with sample results.

options.label: Dithered Press
options.lineage: solar-powered and low-tech web publications: one ink, dithered pictures, a pixel-cut serif
options.thesis: Webshelf printed in one ink. Pictures are dithered into the page's two colours, display type uses a pixel-cut cut of the same serif, and the words you searched for carry an ultramarine underline.
materials: one ink on white (or light ink on near-black)
Redaction serif with its pixel cuts
options.viewport: Your lockup in one ink at top left, the three books turned into three tints; the query set large in the pixel cut on a single heavy rule; numbered results with big pixel numerals in the margin; the topic panel's photo dithered into the page's inks.
options.risk: One ink is austere; it relies on the type and the dithering being done well everywhere, including weather and colour-picker cards that need real colour.

options.label: Raw HTML, Loud
options.lineage: brutalist websites: raw HTML elements at confident sizes
options.thesis: The browser's own vocabulary, turned up: underlined link blue, visited purple, the yellow highlighter of the HTML mark element, black rules and boxed fields, set big enough to look chosen.
options.viewport: Your full-colour lockup beside a boxed search field and a black Search block; a heavy rule; the query restated large with a monospace status line; underlined blue results with highlighted matches; the topic panel in a black box with a greyscale photo.
options.risk: Loud by design: the heavy rules and yellow need restraint on dense pages so it stays fast to scan.

options.label: Browser Grey
options.lineage: 1994 browsers: grey page, bevelled fields, grooved rules
options.thesis: The web as it first looked in a browser: the grey page, sunken fields, raised buttons, grooved rules and Times-style type, done with today's spacing and a proper dark version.
options.viewport: Your full-colour lockup on the grey page beside a sunken search field and a raised Search button; a grooved rule; a numbered list of underlined results; the topic panel as a raised plate with a sunken photo frame.
options.risk: The most nostalgic of the three; bevels everywhere can tip into a costume of an old operating system.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What search engines ship, executed impeccably: white page, centred pill, blue links.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement every visitor expects, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design; close to the version you called rubbish.
